L129: # Liver tumor PDT
L130: 
L131: Photodynamic Therapy for Canine Liver Tumors
L132:

L148: ### Contacts
L149: 
L150: #### Robyn Fox (robynfox@vt.edu), LVT
L151: Clinical Trials Coordinator
L152: ## Purpose
L153: 
L154: To evaluate a new treatment called photodynamic therapy (PDT) for dogs who have been diagnosed with liver tumors.  The goal is to find out if PDT can be done safely, and see if it helps destroy the tumor cells in the liver.  The long-term objective is to develop a minimally invasive way of treating liver tumors.
L155: ## Background
L156: 
L157: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer diagnosed in dogs. While current treatments like radiation and targeted chemotherapy are available, they unfortunately rarely eliminate the tumors completely.  Surgical removal of the tumor and affected portion of the liver remains the standard of care option; however, not every patient is eligible for surgery.
L158: To provide better options for pets, our research team is evaluating a groundbreaking new treatment called Photodynamic Therapy utilizing Light-Activatable Sustained-Exposure Ethanol Injection Technology—or LASEIT-PDT. This innovative technology has the potential to significantly advance how we treat canine liver cancer.
L159: ## Eligibility
L160: 
L161:   * dogs recently diagnosed with a liver tumor
L162:   * dogs whose families have elected surgical removal of the liver tumor
L163: 
L164: ## Exclusion
L165: 
L166:   * Presence of other life-threatening diseases
L167:   * Non-resectable liver tumors
L168: ## Study Design
L169: 
L170: Patients who have undergone a surgical  workup will be deemed eligible for the trial based on CT scan and bloodwork.
L171: 
L172:   * Eligible dogs will undergo the PDT therapy under anesthesia, where a drug called verteporfin is injected into the liver tumor under CT guidance.
L173:   * Dogs will be monitored in the ICU for one night and receive surgery the next day
L174:   * Blood samples will be collected during the hospital stay
L175: ## Compensation
L176: 
L177: Costs associated with diagnosing the liver tumor are not covered by the study.  Once  enrolled, the study covers the cost of PDT treatment, the recheck CT scans, hospital stay charge during the 2-day study period between PDT treatment and liver tumor removal surgery. The study also pays $2000 towards the cost of standard liver tumor removal surgery. The study does not cover costs associated with any complications from PDT treatment. Owners are responsible for their own travel costs.
